cards.title: Does noisy parity learning require Ω(n²/ε²) memory or exponentially many samples?
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants c₁,c₂>0 and n₀ such that, for every integer n≥n₀, every 0<ε<1/2 and every one-pass learner recovering a uniformly random x∈{0,1}^n with probability at least 2/3 from the noisy parity samples defined below, its worst-case memory S and maximum sample count T satisfy S≥c₁n²/ε² or T≥2^{c₂n}? Constants are independent of n, ε and the learner, and ε may tend to zero with n. This states the bounded-error recovery interpretation of Conjecture 1; it does not additionally require a lower bound at exponentially small success probability.
cards.why: Would quantify how observation noise increases the storage needed for a central learning problem, strengthening unconditional limits relevant to streaming learning and bounded-storage cryptography.

references.title: Memory-Sample Lower Bounds for Learning Parity with Noise
references.authors: Garg, Sumegha; Kothari, Pravesh K.; Liu, Pengda; Raz, Ran

cards.definitions: Arithmetic in 𝔽₂={0,1} uses addition and multiplication modulo two; ⟨a,x⟩=Σᵢ₌₁ⁿaᵢxᵢ mod 2. First choose x uniformly from {0,1}^n and hold it fixed. Independently for each t, choose a_t uniformly from {0,1}^n and a noise bit Z_t with Pr[Z_t=1]=1/2−ε; observe (a_t,b_t) with b_t=⟨a_t,x⟩+Z_t mod 2. Noise bits, query vectors and internal learner coins are mutually independent. The learner outputs one estimate x̂; success means x̂=x, and its probability averages over x, all observations and internal coins. The learner sees each sample once in order, cannot choose a_t or revisit discarded observations, and has no computational-time restriction. Formally use a branching program with T+1 layers and width at most 2^S, one start vertex and one outgoing edge for each possible sample at each nonterminal vertex, all going to the next layer. Leaves, possibly in earlier layers, are labelled by estimates in {0,1}^n. Randomized learners may use fresh coins to choose state updates; retained coins are part of the state. Equivalently, the lower bound may be checked on deterministic nonuniform programs, since a random tape can be fixed to achieve at least the average success under this fixed input distribution without increasing width or length. The program may depend on n and ε; its transition description, current layer and input sample are not charged as stored data. Memory counts persistent state bits, S=⌈log₂(width)⌉, and T is the maximum number of consumed samples, not its expectation. No hypothesis is made about the hardness of LPN in unrestricted computation.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the universal bounded-error memory/sample tradeoff with constants uniform in ε, or refute that asymptotic claim by showing that no such constants can work. A bound Ω(n²/ε), a result only for constant ε, or a lower bound in a restricted statistical-query model does not settle the proposed dependence on noise.

context_blocks.title: Noise reduces the information in each equation
context_blocks.text: Without noise, every observation is a correct linear relation about the hidden vector. Here the relation is only slightly more likely to be right than wrong when ε is small. The question asks whether this forces a quadratic loss in the storage threshold as the bias tends to zero.

cards.title: Complexity of choosing a satisfying base in Büchi and p-adic linear arithmetic
cards.formal: Determine the computational complexity of p-existence for each of the two existential logics below. Given one existential formula Φ containing the symbolic base parameter p, decide whether Φ has a satisfying assignment for some integer p≥2 in Büchi arithmetic, or for some prime p in linear arithmetic over p-adic integers. The source proves an NEXP upper bound in both cases and asks whether these bounds can be improved. It does not nominate NP, subexponential time, or another specific improvement. The p-adic infinity conventions and the exact requested complexity precision remain to be fully specified as recorded below.
cards.why: Would determine the cost of choosing a number-theoretic base while solving linear constraints, clarifying how parametric divisibility changes otherwise well-understood existential arithmetic.
cards.status_note: Read the complete MFCS 2021 paper, its author copy and the relevant MFCS 2025 follow-up sections. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution of the two unrestricted p-existence complexity questions. The cited infinity axiom system could not be read in full, so formulation review remains unfinished.

progress.text: Both p-existence problems are shown to lie in NEXP; the conclusion asks whether those upper bounds can be improved.
Restricted valuation-constraint systems at specified primes receive sharper classifications, with a different scope from full p-existence.

importance.reason: A structural boundary for symbolic arithmetic when divisibility bases vary, connecting satisfiability and parameter-dependent number systems. Existing score retained.

sentences: The input is an existential linear-arithmetic formula with a symbolic base p.
The decision asks whether some base makes that formula satisfiable.
Büchi arithmetic allows every integer base at least two, whereas the p-adic variant allows primes.
The source proves NEXP upper bounds and does not obtain the missing classification from its universality hardness theorem.
The exact desired complexity precision and the cited infinity conventions remain to be completed.

cards.definitions: An existential formula is an existential quantifier prefix followed by a quantifier-free Boolean combination of atomic formulas; negation, conjunction and disjunction are allowed. For Büchi arithmetic the domain is ℕ={0,1,…}, the language has constants 0,1, addition, equality and the unary function V_p. For x>0, V_p(x)=p^k where k is the largest nonnegative integer for which p^k divides x; V_p(0)=1. The base p can be composite. For the p-adic variant, p is prime: for a nonzero rational a/b, v_p(a/b) is the exponent of p in a minus that in b. Set |x|_p=p^{−v_p(x)} and |0|_p=0; ℚ_p is the completion of ℚ in this absolute value, and ℤ_p={x∈ℚ_p:v_p(x)≥0}. The valuation extends to ℚ_p and v_p(0)=∞. The logic has two sorts ℤ_p and Z̄=ℤ∪{∞}, constants 0,1 and addition within each sort, equality within each sort, order < on Z̄, and v_p:ℤ_p→Z̄. Finite integers lie below ∞. There is no multiplication of two variables in either logic. Linear constraints may have integer coefficients and constants written in binary, with signed values only where meaningful in the given sort. Semantics of valuation terms involving ∞ are delegated by the source to its cited axiom system and are not yet fully reproduced here. The input is a finite formula with explicit syntax and binary numerals; N is its total bit length. The parameter p itself is not supplied as a binary input integer: v_p or V_p counts as one function symbol, used with the same unknown p throughout Φ. The algorithm decides yes or no, not a numeric approximation, in the uniform Turing bit model. NEXP means nondeterministic time 2^{N^{O(1)}}; no randomized error guarantee replaces correctness.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complexity classification for each full p-existence problem under the recovered source semantics, with upper and hardness bounds that settle the chosen precision. Before certifying a complete benchmark target, finish the infinity conventions and specify what degree of improvement or classification is required. Hardness of p-universality alone does not answer p-existence.

context_blocks.title: The base is itself existentially chosen
context_blocks.text: The formula is fixed as input, but a satisfying interpretation may exist at only some bases. In the p-adic case those bases must be prime; in Büchi arithmetic all integers at least two are eligible. These are different domains within the same base-selection question.

context_blocks.title: Valuations add expressive power to linear arithmetic
context_blocks.text: The formulas can combine addition with constraints on divisibility by powers of the base. In the p-adic language the constraints may compare arbitrary linear expressions in valuations, a broader task than imposing a fixed valuation on each variable.

context_blocks.title: Existence is not the complement of universality
context_blocks.text: The proved coNEXP-completeness result for Büchi arithmetic concerns satisfiability at every base. Negating that outer universal quantifier yields a base where the formula has no satisfying assignment, rather than a base where it does. It therefore does not supply the missing hardness result here.

context_blocks.title: Later restricted cases do not settle base selection
context_blocks.text: The 2025 work gives polynomial-time and NP-completeness results for restricted systems at specified primes, including different behavior at primes two and three. It distinguishes these restrictions from the more expressive Haase–Mansutti setting and does not claim a matching classification for the two full p-existence problems.

context_blocks.title: Remaining formulation work
context_blocks.text: The full semantics for linear valuation terms containing ∞ must be recovered from the primary paper’s reference 17; its axiom system was not available in full during this review, so ordinary extended-real arithmetic is not silently substituted. In addition, “improve NEXP” does not specify a target class or a quantitative time bound; the source should be preserved as a complexity-classification question until the intended completion criterion is fixed.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
